title: Monotonicity of normalized projected variance
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis for real-valued functions on $\Omega$, indexed by a finite nonempty set. For $n\ge 0$, suppose $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is invariant under every permutation of its coordinates, and let $S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfy $1\le |S|\le |T|$. Then the variance, under the product probability measure with marginal $\pi$, of the conditional expectation of $f$ given the coordinates in $S$, divided by $|S|$, is at most the corresponding variance for $T$ divided by $|T|$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$B$ is a finite Fourier basis indexed by a finite nonempty set
$f$ is invariant under all coordinate permutations
